bridge: Builds on M05 metrics, I02 injection and I04 executor boundaries. Required work is a paper/static check only; no live model probes, prompt matrices or model-based scoring are authorised.
teaching:
AI assurance needs a clearly defined security property. An aggregate helpfulness score cannot prove that an agent never sends an unauthorised message. Separate deterministic application controls from probabilistic model behaviour and evaluate their evidence independently.

A small fixed case table can verify a guarded executor without running a model: supply mock proposals and check allow/deny decisions. Real model robustness studies require a separate authorised plan, representative inputs, budget, provider/data permissions and limits on interpretation. A single successful refusal is not proof of general injection resistance.

Unbounded consumption can arise from long inputs, repeated tools, recursive tasks and retries. Enforce limits outside the model and record a bounded failure state. A cost estimate should use published pricing and planned limits rather than sending token-count probes when those are not authorised. The workshop deliberately avoids all billable execution.
example:
Static executor cases (expected)
A read A1 within grant -> allow
A read B1             -> deny ownership
A send email          -> deny unavailable tool
A read A1 after budget exhausted -> deny budget
Missing principal     -> deny authentication
Known harmless task success -> required positive case
No model invocation or inference scoring is needed.
explanation: The table verifies a policy implementation if later translated into isolated mocked unit tests; it does not measure what a model would propose. Keep that distinction in any report. Removing the positive case would allow a deny-everything implementation to appear secure while unusable.
exercise: Hand-check all six cases and write a verification plan identifying the assertion owner, inputs and expected observable result. Define max input bytes, tool count, duration and retry count for a fictional task, without executing a run.
solution: The plan names concrete caps and fails closed when they are reached. Each decision cites policy. It explicitly labels model-behaviour robustness untested, rather than presenting mock proposals as actual model observations.
challenge: Critique “the agent passed100 safety prompts, therefore it is secure.” State missing threat-model/coverage information and design a bounded offline policy check that adds useful evidence without any live evaluation.
challenge_solution: Need authorised scope, attack surfaces, data, action limits, distributions and failure analysis. Offline guarded-executor cases can establish selected enforcement behaviour; they cannot justify a universal model-security claim. Keep the live workload paused until explicitly authorised.
